title: filmstruck.com, from “Coming Soon” to “now closed”
lede: Screenshots of pages saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, stored as images. Click one to open the original capture. The archive’s index listed no successfully saved copy of the home page between September 2017 and December 2018 when we searched it.[^39]

snips.text: “Exclusive streaming home of The Criterion Collection.” “Shown commercial-free and as the director intended.”
“**The largest library of indie films available anywhere.**”
“We regret to inform you that FilmStruck is now closed. Our last day of service was November 29, 2018.”
“FilmStruck was truly a labor of love, and in a world with an abundance of entertainment options – THANK YOU for choosing us.”

note: Film stills inside the screenshots belong to their rights holders and appear only as part of the archived pages.

captures.label: Coming Soon
captures.title: Two days after the announcement
captures.text: A holding page with an email box, a 60-second trailer and four promises: watch anywhere, the exclusive streaming home of the Criterion Collection, rare footage and special features, and no commercials.[^39]

captures.label: Launch week
captures.title: Three days after opening
captures.text: “Hard to find films at your fingertips,” a 14-day free trial, and Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV logos in the how-to-watch panel. The Criterion Channel is offered as an add-on a week before the library leaves Hulu.[^3][^39]

captures.label: Exclusive home
captures.title: A redesigned front page
captures.text: Criterion’s mark leads the page, above a menu of Films, Directors, Ways to Watch and Pricing & Plans. Three months later The Verge published its complaint about the site.[^39][^9]

captures.label: Closed
captures.title: Eight days after the end
captures.text: A single box on a black page, a link to the FAQs and a thank-you. By October 2026 the address forwarded to tcm.com.[^39]
